THE ANCIENT COVENANT RECORD

Volume Six — The Book of Chanokh

THE BOOK OF PARABLES

Why It Is Excluded From This Record

Chapters 37 through 71 in the traditional numbering — the Similitudes — not carried in this record

METHODOLOGY OF THIS RECORD

Physical Verification.  Only ancient Chanokh texts used are physically verified on the pre-Christian Aramaic leather of the Dead Sea Scrolls (4Q201, 4Q208, 4Q209).

Strict Chronology.  The later narrative chapters are removed because they contain internal historical markers from the Hellenistic and Maccabean eras, and my focus is strictly on the oldest, pre-exilic core layers.

Linguistic Independence.  The Ge’ez Orit is used to analyze the creation and legal frameworks because its Semitic grammar preserves the feminine Ruach and the legal office of ha-satan, completely exposing late Western theological alterations.

WHY THESE CHAPTERS ARE EXCLUDED

The Book of Parables is an independent literary block that was dropped into the middle of the Chanokh corpus long after the Dead Sea Scrolls were archived.

These chapters do not appear in any Dead Sea Scrolls manuscript — the only section of the entire Book of Chanokh missing from the ancient record.

Within these chapters, YHWH’s name is systematically erased and replaced with the title “Lord of Spirits” over one hundred times. The original pre-Rabbinic, pre-Christian covenant texts do not contain this substitution. This is a scribal alteration of the divine name, not original covenant language.

These chapters also take the phrase “one like a son of man” from a vision in the Book of Daniyyel — a human figure in a prophetic dream — and inflate it into a cosmic heavenly judge hidden since before creation. That is not what Daniyyel’s text says. It is scribal invention: a new theological construct built by expanding a single covenant image beyond anything the original text described.

Roman-era NT writers then mined this scribal construction — not the original covenant texts — to assemble their invented deity. The manipulation trail runs from the scribal additions in these chapters directly into the NT’s fabricated claims. These chapters are the manipulation layer. They are excluded from this record because they document what Second Temple scribes invented, not what the original covenant tradition preserved.

The following chapters — renumbered from their original Ge’ez Orit position — return to the pre-Second Temple, pre-Christian, pre-Rabbinic primary text.
